GLMs

  1. The data in stork.txt display the stress-induced corticosterone levels circulating in the blood of European white storks and their survival over the subsequent five years of study. Analyze the data following this structure: 1. Question, 2. Exploratory analyses, 3. Fit model, 4. Validate model, 5. Test hypothesis and assess explanatory power, and 6. Communication of results (plot + description of main results).

Question: Does corticosterone level predict survival of European white storks over a period of 5 years?

#Exploratory analyses
stork <- read.table("../data_raw/stork.txt", header = T)

ggplot(stork, aes(x = Corticosterone, y = Survival))+
  geom_point()

Fit Model:

stork.glm<-glm(Survival ~ Corticosterone, family=binomial(link="logit"), data = stork)
summary(stork.glm)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = Survival ~ Corticosterone, family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
##     data = stork)
## 
## Coefficients:
##                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)  
## (Intercept)     2.70304    1.74725   1.547   0.1219  
## Corticosterone -0.07980    0.04368  -1.827   0.0677 .
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 45.234  on 33  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 41.396  on 32  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 45.396
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4

Validate Model:

simulateResiduals(stork.glm, plot = T)

## Object of Class DHARMa with simulated residuals based on 250 simulations with refit = FALSE . See ?DHARMa::simulateResiduals for help. 
##  
## Scaled residual values: 0.6634103 0.7655982 0.8465965 0.8503342 0.6259939 0.8893231 0.7981121 0.8486897 0.7876165 0.8626401 0.9436615 0.840748 0.9343146 0.2100377 0.1285811 0.03841849 0.1588645 0.3212054 0.2972712 0.1469927 ...

Test hypothesis and assess explanatory power:

anova(stork.glm, test = "LRT")
## Analysis of Deviance Table
## 
## Model: binomial, link: logit
## 
## Response: Survival
## 
## Terms added sequentially (first to last)
## 
## 
##                Df Deviance Resid. Df Resid. Dev Pr(>Chi)  
## NULL                              33     45.234           
## Corticosterone  1   3.8382        32     41.396   0.0501 .
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
r2(stork.glm)
## # R2 for Logistic Regression
##   Tjur's R2: 0.102

Communicate results: Animals with lower corticosterone levels have a higher rate of survival (-0.07980, Chisq = 3.8382, p-value 0.0501). The model explained 10% of the variance.

ggplot(aes(x=Corticosterone, y=Survival), data=stork)+
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.9)+
  geom_smooth(method=glm, method.args = list(family = "binomial"), se=T)+
  theme_classic()
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

  1. The clusters.txt dataset contains the response variable Cancers (the number of reported cancer cases per clinic) and the explanatory variable Distance (the distance from a nuclear plant to the clinic in kilometers). Analyze the data following this structure: 1. Question, 2. Exploratory analyses, 3. Fit model, 4. Validate model, 5. Test hypothesis and assess explanatory power, and 6. Communication of results (plot + description of main results).

1.) Question: Do cancer cases occur more often closer to a nuclear power plant?

#2.) Exploratory analyses

cancer <- read.table("../data_raw/clusters.txt", header = T)

ggplot(data = cancer, aes(x = Cancers))+
  geom_histogram(color = "white", fill = "black")
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

3.) Fit model

cancer.glm <- glm(Cancers ~ Distance, data = cancer, family = poisson)
summary(cancer.glm)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = Cancers ~ Distance, family = poisson, data = cancer)
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)  
## (Intercept)  0.186865   0.188728   0.990   0.3221  
## Distance    -0.006138   0.003667  -1.674   0.0941 .
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for poisson family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 149.48  on 93  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 146.64  on 92  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 262.41
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 5

Validate Model:

simulateResiduals(cancer.glm, plot = T)

## Object of Class DHARMa with simulated residuals based on 250 simulations with refit = FALSE . See ?DHARMa::simulateResiduals for help. 
##  
## Scaled residual values: 0.03429555 0.3909649 0.3629404 0.02236689 0.356397 0.2311206 0.2336816 0.2710443 0.385886 0.428745 0.05798994 0.1826207 0.433612 0.1793212 0.01159758 0.3505102 0.06116024 0.1559253 0.2506516 0.3347125 ...
testDispersion(cancer.glm, plot = T)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.6357, p-value < 2.2e-16
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
cancer.nb <- glm.nb(Cancers ~ Distance, data=cancer)
summary(cancer.nb)
## 
## Call:
## glm.nb(formula = Cancers ~ Distance, data = cancer, init.theta = 1.359466981, 
##     link = log)
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
## (Intercept)  0.182490   0.252434   0.723    0.470
## Distance    -0.006041   0.004727  -1.278    0.201
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for Negative Binomial(1.3595) family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 96.647  on 93  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 94.973  on 92  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 253.19
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 1
## 
## 
##               Theta:  1.359 
##           Std. Err.:  0.612 
## 
##  2 x log-likelihood:  -247.191

Test hypotheses and assess explanatory power:

simulateResiduals(cancer.nb, plot = T)

## Object of Class DHARMa with simulated residuals based on 250 simulations with refit = FALSE . See ?DHARMa::simulateResiduals for help. 
##  
## Scaled residual values: 0.1691706 0.08785123 0.2964165 0.1319477 0.5308209 0.07382625 0.1803357 0.3979211 0.2507544 0.1048807 0.1318335 0.07170322 0.5260157 0.2110324 0.1405788 0.424706 0.076321 0.02451732 0.4505731 0.1809262 ...
testDispersion(cancer.nb, plot = T)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 0.96172, p-value = 0.976
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
anova(cancer.nb, test = "LRT")
## Warning in anova.negbin(cancer.nb, test = "LRT"): tests made without
## re-estimating 'theta'

## Model: Negative Binomial(1.3595), link: log

## Response: Cancers

## Terms added sequentially (first to last)

##          Df Deviance Resid. Df Resid. Dev Pr(>Chi)
## NULL                        93     96.647         
## Distance  1   1.6741        92     94.973   0.1957
r2(cancer.nb)
## # R2 for Generalized Linear Regression
##   Nagelkerke's R2: 0.027

Communicate Results:

There is no significant relationship between number of cancer cases and distance from a nuclear power plant. (Chisq = 1.6741, p value 0.19). The model explained 2.7% of the variance. Based on these results, we cannot conclude that living closer to a power plant increases the number of reported cancer cases.

ggplot(data = cancer, aes(x = Distance, y = Cancers)) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "poisson"), color = "red") +
  labs(x =  "Distance from nuclear power plant", y = "Cancer cases count")+
  theme_classic()
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

Question 3: Use data(cbpp) from library(lme4) to model the number of cases of cattle plague (incidence) as a function of period. Control for herd size in your model. Analyze the data following this structure: 1. Question, 2. Exploratory analyses, 3. Fit model, 4. Validate model, 5. Test hypothesis and assess explanatory power, and 6. Communication of results (plot + description of main results).

Question: Is the number of cases of cattle plague influenced by time period or herd size?

#Exploratory analyses
plague <- cbpp

ggplot(plague, aes(x = incidence, y = size))+
  geom_point()

ggplot(plague, aes(x = incidence, y = period))+
  geom_point()

Fit Model

plague_glmm <- glmer(cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd), 
                    data = plague, 
                    family = binomial)
summary(plague_glmm)
## Generalized linear mixed model fit by maximum likelihood (Laplace
##   Approximation) [glmerMod]
##  Family: binomial  ( logit )
## Formula: cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd)
##    Data: plague
## 
##       AIC       BIC    logLik -2*log(L)  df.resid 
##     194.1     204.2     -92.0     184.1        51 
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -2.3816 -0.7889 -0.2026  0.5142  2.8791 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  herd   (Intercept) 0.4123   0.6421  
## Number of obs: 56, groups:  herd, 15
## 
## Fixed effects:
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)  -1.3983     0.2312  -6.048 1.47e-09 ***
## period2      -0.9919     0.3032  -3.272 0.001068 ** 
## period3      -1.1282     0.3228  -3.495 0.000474 ***
## period4      -1.5797     0.4220  -3.743 0.000182 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##         (Intr) perid2 perid3
## period2 -0.363              
## period3 -0.340  0.280       
## period4 -0.260  0.213  0.198

Validate Model

simulateResiduals(plague_glmm, plot = T)

## Object of Class DHARMa with simulated residuals based on 250 simulations with refit = FALSE . See ?DHARMa::simulateResiduals for help. 
##  
## Scaled residual values: 0.3973751 0.8945491 0.9956805 0.402695 0.2901473 0.3724286 0.2717665 0.8740848 0.649741 0.2680626 0.8285526 0.4657061 0.2801929 0.9017911 0.2280075 0.6641468 0.03069543 0.111195 0.8066431 0.4864031 ...

Test hypothesis and assess explanatory power:

drop1(plague_glmm, test = "Chisq")
## Single term deletions
## 
## Model:
## cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd)
##        npar    AIC   LRT   Pr(Chi)    
## <none>      194.05                    
## period    3 213.66 25.61 1.151e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
r2(plague_glmm)
## # R2 for Mixed Models
## 
##   Conditional R2: 0.776
##      Marginal R2: 0.354

Communicate Results: The model revealed a significant primary effect of period on disease incidence (chisq = 25.61, df = 3, p < 0.001). All subsequent periods after baseline (Period 1) showed a marked reduction in the probability of infection.

pred <- estimate_relation(plague_glmm) #modelbased
pred.farm <- estimate_relation(plague_glmm, include_random = T)

ggplot(pred.farm, aes(x=herd, y=Predicted, group=period))+
  geom_line(color="darkgrey", alpha=0.6)+
  geom_point(data = plague, aes(x=herd, y=size, color = period), size=0.9, alpha=0.6, position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.05))+
  geom_line(data = pred, aes(x = period, y = Predicted, color=period), linewidth = 2)+
  geom_ribbon(data = pred, aes(x = period, ymin = CI_low, ymax = CI_high, fill=period), alpha = 0.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("firebrick4", "dodgerblue3", "green", "pink"))+
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("firebrick4", "dodgerblue3", "green", "pink"))+
  facet_wrap(~period)+
  ylab("Herd size")+
  xlab("Incidence of plague")+
  theme_classic()
## `geom_line()`: Each group consists of only one observation.
## ℹ Do you need to adjust the group aesthetic?
## `geom_line()`: Each group consists of only one observation.
## ℹ Do you need to adjust the group aesthetic?
## `geom_line()`: Each group consists of only one observation.

Question 4: Use insects.csv to model the number of insects (count) as an additive function (no interaction) of habitat (categorical) and flowers (numerical). Previous studies have reported that habitat quality tends to drive the detection of insects (some habitats have no insects regardless of flowers). Analyze the data following this structure: 1. Question, 2. Exploratory analyses, 3. Fit model, 4. Validate model, 5. Test hypothesis and assess explanatory power, and 6. Communication of results (plot + description of main results).

Question: Is the number of insects counted correlated with habitat type and number of flowers present?

#Exploratory analyses
insects <- read.csv("../data_raw/insects.csv", header = T)

insects$flowers <- as.factor(insects$flowers)

ggplot(insects, aes(x = flowers, y = count)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~habitat)

Fit Model

insect.model <- glm(count ~ habitat + flowers,
             family = poisson(link = "log"),
             data = insects)

summary(insect.model)
